evals.query: Here's every request we have for our team calendar app (attached). One team, six weeks. What do we do first?
expected_behavior: Opens with a one-sentence headline naming the single bet that matters most now and why
Writes a short ranked list of problems first (tied to retention of teams of 10 or more), noting that none was agreed, and maps each request to a problem or marks it as serving none

Keeps a large uncertain bet in play: focus blocks (3) get a cheap test or a speculative slot rather than losing to small items, or the answer says explicitly that Now holds only small work and what would change that
Orders by dependency and learning: the recurring events rewrite (2) comes before time zone suggestions (6) and room booking (9)
Gives each Now bet an appetite and a stop rule, and lists a Not doing section with a reason per item (for example emoji reactions, custom colours, animated tour)

Follows the output structure: Headline, Problems in order, a Now table (Bet, Problem it serves, Appetite, Stop if), Next with what each waits for, Later as direction only, Not doing, and Mix as rough shares

evals.query: The board wants a 12-month roadmap for our recipe app with a delivery date for every feature. Can you lay it out month by month? Features so far: meal plans, grocery delivery integration, video recipes, pantry tracking, social cooking challenges, offline mode.
expected_behavior: Pushes back on dated features twelve months out in one or two sentences, and proposes Now, Next and Later instead
Lays it out as Now, Next and Later sections, not months, with decreasing detail: a Now table that is specific and committed, Next outlined with what each waits for, Later as direction only
Uses dates only where the world sets one (for example an external partner deadline or a seasonal moment), not on every item
Frames bets as problems and outcomes for teams to solve rather than a list of features to ship
Sizes Now bets by appetite (the most time each is worth) rather than by estimate, and gives each a stop rule
Asks for or writes the ranked list of problems before ordering the features, since the request gives none

evals.query: One sprint left before the holidays on our fitness class booking app. Sales wants calendar export for a prospect, support wants the waitlist bug fixed (people get booked into full classes), and design wants to redesign the home screen. I can only do one well. Which?
expected_behavior: Answers with a recommendation in the first line and commits to it
Judges by opportunity cost (what each option displaces and whether it is the best use of the sprint) rather than scoring each for return
States the trade-off for the requests not chosen in the form 'this, if that waits', rather than a flat no
Puts the unchosen items under Next or Not doing as 'item · reason' lines, so each is answered rather than left to come back
Gives the chosen bet a stop rule or checkpoint
Leaves the priority call the user owns (for example whether the prospect deal outweighs the bug) as one line to ask afterwards, not decided silently or written up as a long section

trigger_checks.query: We have far more requests than capacity for Q2 on our podcast app. What goes first?
Build us a Now, Next, Later roadmap for the habit tracker from this list of ideas.
Sales and support want different things next sprint on our meal-planning app. How do I decide what to build first?
Is adding voice notes to our journaling app worth doing at all?
What should success look like for voice notes, and how do we measure it?
Turn these 200 app store reviews of our weather app into a list of actions.
